sections.h2: Where do Wilkes County property owners take tax questions?
sections.html:
Tax Administration is in the Wilkes County Offices, 110 North Street, Wilkesboro. The appraisal department takes revaluation and appeal calls at 336-651-7301 on weekdays between 8:30 AM and 5:00 PM. Appeals staff are on the second floor, per the county's appeals FAQ.

The Tax Administration page collects the tools in one place: online payment options, a parcel and real property search, GIS maps, personal property forms, occupancy tax information and the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Listings department: personal property and business listings
  • Appraisal department: assessed value and appeals
  • Online payment link: bills for the current year

sections.h2: How big was the 2025 revaluation in Wilkes County?
sections.html:
Wilkes County's last revaluation before 2025 was in 2019, and the county estimated that real property values rose about 75% to 80% overall as of January 1, 2025. Its press release notes the spread was wide, and that the figures were estimates that could change before notices went out.

The county mailed notices on March 17, 2025, showing land and structure values as of January 1, 2025. Owners with present use value land saw both the use value and the gross land value on the notice.

The release also says higher values do not turn into a proportional tax increase, since the county, fire districts and municipalities set their rates in June. Wilkes reappraises more often than the eight year minimum that state law requires.

sections.h2: How did appeals work after the 2025 notices in Wilkes County?
sections.html:
Owners filed online after getting a change of value notice, attaching supporting documents. The 2025 portal closed at 5 p.m. on May 2, 2025.

The county's appeals FAQ says the review period could run to December 1 of a revaluation year, and hearings can go later. If you had a bill but no decision yet, a later reduction applies back to the 2025 bill, and a paid bill that is cut produces a refund.

The FAQ also covers timing of payment. The 1.5% discount for paying by August 31 was still available to owners with an appeal pending, as long as payment came before September 1, and interest did not begin until January 6, 2026.

At the state level, a property owner can ask the county board for a hearing before it adjourns, and a Property Tax Commission appeal must be filed within 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-322, G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What bill dates and penalties apply in Wilkes County?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1 under G.S. 105-360, and a payment made before January 6 carries no interest. From January 6 to February 1 the charge is 2%, and after that it is three-quarters of one percent for each month.

Listing runs through January 31 unless extended. For 2026 the commissioners moved the personal property listing deadline to March 2, 2026, per the Tax Administration page. Ask the listings department what the current year's deadline is.

sections.h2: What relief programs does Wilkes County administer?
sections.html:
The county names three: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferment. Applications are on the county's forms page or from the tax office. The county release gave June 2, 2025 as that year's cutoff.

  • Elderly or disabled: greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran: first $45,000 of appraised value, no age or income test (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: 4% of income, or 5% in the upper band, with the excess deferred as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

The 2026 income limit printed by the Department of Revenue is $38,800 on its AV-9 form. Only one program can be used per owner.

sections.h2: How should I handle unpaid tax when selling in Wilkes County?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches as of the January 1 listing date (G.S. 105-355), so the buyer's lawyer expects it cleared by closing. If it goes unpaid, the county can foreclose and sell at auction, and you can redeem before confirmation by paying tax, penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374).

Two practical steps help. Ask the tax office for the full amount owed, and tell your closing attorney if a circuit breaker deferral is on the parcel, since the deferred years become due when you sell.

sections.h2: Which Wilkes County communities and townships does the county revaluation cover?
sections.html:
The county's release breaks results out by four towns, North Wilkesboro, Wilkesboro, Ronda and Elkin, and by townships including Broadway, Mountain View, Moravian Falls, Mulberry-Fairplains, Pleasant Hill, Traphill, Boomer, Champion, Austin, Millers Creek, Arlington, State Road, Knotville, Roaring River, Cricket, Brushy Mountain, Buck Shoals, Wilbar, Goshen and McGrady.

If your house sits inside a town, you have town and county tax on the same bill, and a fire district may add its own. Rates come from separate boards, so ask the tax office which districts apply to your parcel number.

The release says tax bills for 2025 were expected to be mailed by August 4, 2025. Bills in other years follow the same statutory September 1 due date.

sections.h2: What should a Wilkes County seller ask the tax office?
sections.html:
Call 336-651-7301 or visit Tax Administration with the parcel number and ask a short list of questions. The answers decide what your closing attorney holds back from your proceeds.

  • What is the current year's balance, and has the bill been mailed?
  • Is any appeal on the parcel still undecided?
  • Is there a relief program deferral, such as the circuit breaker, on the account?
  • Is present use value land part of the sale?
  • Which fire or town districts apply?

The county's FAQ confirms that a pending appeal does not pause the bill. Pay by the due date and let any reduction come back as a refund.

Wilkes County also offers online tax payment, and the Tax Administration page links to the Board of Equalization and Review meeting information. Save the payment receipt for the closing file.

faqs.q: What is the date of the latest Wilkes County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county completed a revaluation in 2025, effective January 1, 2025, and its previous one was in 2019. It estimated a countywide increase of 75% to 80%, varying by property.

faqs.q: Does an open appeal cost me the Wilkes County early payment discount?
faqs.a: For 2025, yes. The county said the 1.5% discount applied if the bill was paid before September 1, even with an appeal pending. Ask the tax office whether a discount applies to the current year.

faqs.q: What happens if Wilkes County lowers my value after I paid?
faqs.a: You get a refund of the overpayment. The county's appeals FAQ states that a reduction on appeal applies back to the bill for that year.

faqs.q: Is there an interest-free period on Wilkes County bills?
faqs.a: Yes. Bills are due September 1, but under G.S. 105-360 no interest accrues until January 6. After that, 2% applies to February 1, then three-quarters of a percent monthly.

faqs.q: Does Wilkes County offer help for disabled veterans?
faqs.a: Yes. The county lists a disabled veteran exclusion, which removes the first $45,000 of appraised value under state law. File with the county assessor and ask the tax office for the current form.
